recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-14700 unless a human wants to separately review unrelated terminology-service examples that mention SNOMED CT/Myocardial infarction.
issue_request: FHIR-14700 was a Published FHIR-core ValueSet change request from the January 2018 ballot, resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked whether a SNOMED CT example in the ValueSet $validate-code request was really a subsumption test and directed removal of the extraneous text, including the SNOMED CT implicit value set URL.
initial_application: The issue was pre-applied in SVN revision 13351, represented in git as d90f55e1cbc897c77c5188342e1d43353f38f2c3. That commit removed the exact seven-line SNOMED CT example from source/valueset/$validate-code-request.txt and made related non-substantive ValueSet documentation updates.
additional_context: ValueSet remains an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini, and source/valueset/operationdefinition-ValueSet-validate-code.xml still includes source/valueset/$validate-code-request.txt as the authoritative request example. The current request example file contains only the simple LOINC validation and CodeableConcept examples; exact searches found none of the removed 399211009 / fhir_vs%3Disa/22298006 wording in the active ValueSet operation sources. Zulip and Confluence searches found no substantive community discussion that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the requested removal is already present in the current active source and the remaining SNOMED CT/Myocardial examples elsewhere are different terminology-service examples, not the invalid ValueSet $validate-code subsumption-looking request identified by FHIR-14700.
